themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street vendor complaints spiked to 11 THIS WEEK vs. a baseline average of 1.4 per week—a 700% increase (z-score: 7.31)—suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown, vendor proliferation, or new complaint awareness in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 11 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
No contextual news or community board discussion available to explain driver
reporting_angles: Is NYPD or DOC stepping up enforcement in the district? Interview vendors and enforcement officials.
Are complaints coming from specific blocks (e.g., near Columbia University or transit hubs)? Map the complaints.

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Explode
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violations jumped to 4 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating either new park activity or enforcement issues.
evidence: 4 park rules violation complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
1500% spike with z-score of 8.66 (highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Community board has requested park reconstruction/upgrades but no recent enforcement activity documented
reporting_angles: Which parks (Morningside Park, St. Nicholas Terrace Park, etc.) are affected? What rules are being violated?
Did Parks Department change enforcement or did park conditions deteriorate, attracting violations?

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints surged to 31 two weeks ago vs. a 5.9 weekly average—a 428% spike (z-score: 7.08)—suggesting widespread outages or a systemic maintenance failure affecting public safety and evening foot traffic.
evidence: 31 street light complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
428% spike with z-score of 7.08 (highly statistically significant)
Community board has standing request for DOT capital investment in infrastructure, suggesting chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Which blocks are dark? Is this a specific substation failure or widespread grid issue? Interview Con Edison and DOT.
How long have lights been out? Are residents reporting safety concerns or crime increases in unlit areas?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints nearly tripled to 152 two weeks ago vs. a 54.1 weekly average—a 181% surge (z-score: 4.05)—pointing to either construction activity, street events, or new outdoor vendor/performer activity.
evidence: 152 street/sidewalk noise complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 54.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Timing overlaps with vendor enforcement spike, suggesting possible enforcement-related activity or new street market presence
reporting_angles: Is there active construction or street work (e.g., subway renovation, street resurfacing) driving noise complaints?
Are vendors, street performers, or outdoor events concentrated on specific blocks? Cross-reference with vendor complaint locations.

themes_detail.label: Residential Garbage & Illegal Dumping Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints and illegal dumping combined are showing sustained elevation: 8 disposal complaints 3 WEEKS AGO (220% above baseline) and 10 dumping complaints 2 WEEKS AGO (220% above baseline)—indicating possible waste management breakdown or lax enforcement.
evidence: 8 residential disposal complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.5 weekly average (220% spike, z-score: 5.5)
10 illegal dumping complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 3.1 weekly average (220% spike, z-score: 4.48)
Spike pattern suggests either reduced Sanitation pickups or contractor issues; no recent community board discussion available
reporting_angles: Has Sanitation Department reduced pickup frequency or routes in this district? Interview DSNY.
Are specific blocks accumulating garbage? Is this tied to new construction (374 DOB permits filed in 90 days) blocking street access?
